assets.title: Copper lead
assets.description: Low front three-quarter hero, warm copper shell and upright green sail against cool soft bark.
assets.composition: Output: one landscape cover, 630:500 aspect ratio, preferably render 1260x1000 or larger in that ratio. Low front THREE-QUARTER macro view: hero ant walks toward the lower-left foreground, head at about (32%,58%), rounded dark gaster at (74%,48%). Hero spans most of the width, feet at 88-93% height and antenna tips near 36-40%; ant alone about 53% frame height. All six legs readable, three on each side; full ant not cropped. Upright leaf rises from mandibles into upper-left/upper-center, top at 8%, broad green blade separated from body and not larger than the ant. Bark supports the bottom; calm blue-grey canopy blur across top. Thin cyan trace recedes behind the gaster toward upper-right with three tiny soft workers. Strong copper silhouette and broad soft highlights, hero tack-sharp, background gently defocused.
assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: finished itch store-page key art for a restrained stylized 3D leafcutter-ant game.
Primary request: the FOREGROUND ANT IS THE HERO, CLOSE, LARGE, SHARP AND IMMEDIATELY READABLE EVEN AS A SMALL THUMBNAIL. Camera is low at ant-eye height, in a macro close-up. Entire ant, all feet, both antennae and upright leaf remain inside the frame. Ant alone excluding carried leaf occupies roughly 40-60 percent of image height; do not satisfy this size using the leaf alone. The foreground ant is the largest recognizable discrete subject, while the leaf supports its silhouette.
Input images: image 1 is current in-game material reference: use ONLY THE LEFT COLUMN A ant, copper head/thorax and darker mahogany gaster. Ignore B and old-look columns, all labels and HUD. Image 2 is mesh anatomy/shape reference: broad simple head, small black eyes, elongated lightly spined thorax, small two-node waist, rounded gaster, articulated cylindrical legs, elbowed antennae. Use image 1 A colors over image 2 old uniform material. Images 3 and 4 are environment references ONLY: match grey-green shallow elongated bark plates, broad flat olive moss patches and thin cyan surface scent trace. Their tiny-ant composition is superseded by this new close framing. These are references for a NEW artwork, not edit targets or layouts to copy.
Subject/materials: one leafcutter with copper-rust head and thorax, distinctly darker mahogany-brown rounded gaster, medium reddish-brown legs. Glossy smooth shell, large soft broad daylight highlights, clear color separation from cool background, simple game-mesh forms. No black silhouette, no uniform brown plastic, no photoreal hair or shell microdetail. Keep the head and thorax large and clearly recognizable, tiny dark eyes and plausible mandibles, no cartoon human face.
Anatomy/action: exactly SIX jointed legs, THREE legs per side, attached to the THORAX, never to abdomen or head; arrange far-side feet with plausible offsets for readable separation. Exactly TWO elbowed antennae emerging from the head, distinct from the legs. Small two-node waist connecting thorax to rounded gaster. The head points in the walking direction, gaster behind. One plain green cut LEAF FRAGMENT, broad flat simple leaf blade, lower cut edge gripped directly BETWEEN THE MANDIBLES in front of the head; fragment rises UPRIGHT above the head like a sail. Leaf does not obscure eyes, thorax or legs. No long stalk, no carrying in forelegs, no horizontal leaf or whole branch.
Scene/backdrop: an ordinary enormous tree at millimetre scale, shown close enough that shallow grey-green / weathered grey-brown procedural bark plates recede in perspective. Flat olive moss patches, sparse simple leaf/branch shapes far back, blue-grey sky or canopy bokeh. The image should feel like an attractive real-time 3D game render with macro depth of field, clean large shapes and restrained detail. No wood-scan realism, deep ravines, fluffy moss or lush fantasy vegetation.
Supporting action: a SINGLE thin translucent cyan scent trace hugs the bark and curves away BEHIND the hero into the softer background, bark visible through it, no neon bloom, floating cable, magical beam or built road. Exactly three very small distant leaf-carrying workers spaced along this trace. Each distant worker faces the direction it walks, head and upright leaf AHEAD and rounded gaster behind; all follow the route toward the foreground hero, never backward-walking ants. They must remain small and less detailed, subordinate to the big foreground ant.
Lighting/style: soft warm daylight on copper, cool sky fill, broad satin-gloss highlights, modest natural contact shadows. Focus on head, thorax, waist, gaster and six legs; shallow depth of field softens backdrop and distant workers without blurring the hero. Readable game-art polish, no extreme lens distortion.
Constraints: completely NO TEXT, letters, numbers, logos, trademarks, watermarks, UI, borders or collage. No invented structures, weapons, clothing, other animals, birds, extra foreground insects or fantasy objects. Do not reproduce labels or interface from any reference.

Upright leaf rises from mandibles into upper-left/upper-center, top at 8%, broad green blade separated from body and not larger than the ant. Bark supports the bottom; calm blue-grey canopy blur across top. Thin cyan trace recedes behind the gaster toward upper-right with three tiny soft workers. Strong copper silhouette and broad soft highlights, hero tack-sharp, background gently defocused.
assets.export_operation: Lanczos downsample with only centered sub-percent aspect-ratio trim; no creative postprocessing.

iterations.reason: Initial generation had only five clearly visible legs; added a distinct far-side foreleg.
iterations.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET, the Copper lead cover. Image 2 is supporting anatomy reference only. Correct ONE anatomical omission in image 1: the hero presently has only five clearly visible legs. Give the foreground ant EXACTLY SIX LEGS, three on each side of the thorax. Keep its existing three near-side legs and two visible far-side legs, and ADD ONE slender reddish-brown far-side FORELEG attached beneath the FRONT of the thorax, partly behind the head, bending downward and forward-left to a separate bark contact point between the existing extreme-left foreground foot and the existing middle far-side foot. This new sixth leg must be clearly distinguishable from the legs already present and from both antennae. Plausible jointed structure matching the existing smooth game-mesh legs; no leg attached to head or gaster. Preserve everything else: current 1.26:1 canvas and camera, large sharp copper-rust head and thorax, darker mahogany gaster, broad soft gloss, exactly two antennae, current five other legs, leaf clamped upright in mandibles, bark, olive moss, soft sky and three small background workers and cyan trace. Only add the missing sixth leg and its small contact shadow. Do not zoom out, reduce ant size, move the leaf or redesign the ant. No text, logos, trademarks or watermark.
iterations.result: Six distinct jointed legs; other composition/materials retained.

assets.visual_validation: Inspected master and final export: dominant sharp copper-rust hero, darker mahogany gaster, six legs, two elbowed antennae, upright leaf held at mandibles, softer small background workers/trail, no text/logo/trademark.

assets.title: Moss sail
assets.description: Low near-side three-quarter profile with separated reddish legs, dark gaster and cooler moss backdrop.
assets.composition: Output: one landscape cover, 630:500 aspect ratio, preferably render 1260x1000 or larger in that ratio. Low near-side THREE-QUARTER PROFILE macro view, close enough for the copper ant to dominate. Head on left at (29%,58%), dark mahogany gaster on right at (76%,48%). Hero walking to the LEFT, along a slightly rising shallow bark plate. Whole body and six legs span x=10-92%; three near-side legs and three offset far-side legs, antenna tips at about y=38%, feet near y=91%, ant alone about 53% height. The flat upright leaf gripped between the mandibles rises to y=9% at upper-left; keep it narrow enough to reveal the head, and the leaf is smaller than the full ant. Soft cooler olive moss and grey-green plates behind, calm pale canopy blur. A small cyan scent trace bends behind the gaster into upper-right depth with three very tiny workers walking toward the hero, head-first. Warm broad shell highlights preserve clear copper head/thorax and darker mahogany gaster; rich warm subject against muted cool surroundings.

assets.title: Leafline close
assets.description: Close frontal three-quarter ant approaching the viewer, with a softly receding branch route.
assets.composition: Output: one landscape cover, 630:500 aspect ratio, preferably render 1260x1000 or larger in that ratio. Low FRONTAL THREE-QUARTER macro view with foreground ant approaching camera and slightly to the RIGHT, copper head at (62%,58%) and mahogany gaster behind at (31%,44%). Body not head-on symmetric: show its long thorax and waist clearly. Six distinct leg silhouettes extend across x=10-94%, antenna tips around y=35%, feet y=91%, ant alone about 56% height. Flat leaf sail rises from lower cut edge between the jaws at the right of the head to upper-right at y=7%, without obscuring the shell, eyes or antennae. Soft pale blue-grey canopy and shallow grey-green bark, flat olive patches; single huge branch is only a muted out-of-focus backdrop. Thin cyan scent trace recedes behind the dark gaster toward upper-left, with three very small soft workers following head-first toward camera. Clean rounded game-mesh forms, warm copper glossy highlights, fully sharp hero. No large branch junction competing with the ant.

assets.composition: Output: one ultra-wide panoramic banner, aspect ratio 1920:620 (3.097:1), preferably render 2400x775 or higher, compose for this extreme-wide frame from the start.
